newsitem.title: USA: Lukens starts up anneal and pickle line.
newsitem.headline: Lukens starts up anneal and pickle line.

text.p: Lukens Inc said Wednesday it has started up the world's largest anneal and pickle line at its facility in Massillon.

"With production beginning on this advanced-technology finishing line, Lukens becomes the first specialty steelmaker to process stainless steel plate in coils up to 96-inches wide," said chief executive R.W. Van Sant.
"The product's extra width and superior quality attributes will deliver attractive benefits for customers striving to improve yields and productivity, while lowering their costs."

The wide anneal and pickle line has processed more than 300 trial coils of grade 304 and 304L stainless steel plate at thicknesses of 3/16-inch to 1/2-inch and in widths of 48 inches to 98.5 inches. The line's commissioning program should be completed by the third quarter. The system's annual capacity is rated at about 120,000 tons when full production levels are achieved.

Annealing is a heat treatment process that softens stainless steel and changes its metallurgical structure to impart corrosion and temperature resistant properties. Pickling is a chemical treatment process that cleans stainless steel surfaces and adds corrosion resistance.
